# Process Tailoring Rules

**AI-generated by:** Alson (A.I Agent) on behalf of Agno JF

PMBOK 8 treats the processes as illustrative and nonprescriptive. Tailoring selects the smallest useful set and level of rigor for the project.

## Tailoring Factors

Assess the factors below before selecting process rigor:

| Factor | Questions |
|---|---|
| Criticality | What is the consequence of failure or noncompliance? |
| Scale | How large are the scope, team, budget, and number of interfaces? |
| Duration | How long will the work run and how often will conditions change? |
| Complexity | How many unknowns, dependencies, stakeholders, and technical interfaces exist? |
| Approach | Is the project predictive, adaptive, or hybrid? |
| Standards | What legal, regulatory, contractual, or organizational rules apply? |
| Culture | How are decisions, collaboration, and escalation normally handled? |
| Maturity | What existing methods, data, templates, and controls are available? |

## Dispositions

| Disposition | Use when | Required record |
|---|---|---|
| Required | The process protects value, compliance, a baseline, or a material decision. | Purpose, owner, trigger, minimum output |
| Conditional | The process becomes necessary when a stated trigger occurs. | Trigger, review date, fallback action |
| Not needed | The project context makes the process unnecessary and the risk is acceptable. | Reason, decision maker, review trigger |

## Rigor Levels

| Level | Minimum practice |
|---|---|
| Lightweight | One clear owner, short record, decision or trigger visible. |
| Standard | Defined inputs, documented output, source traceability, review point. |
| Formal | Baseline, approval path, independent review, audit trail, and change control. |

Do not equate adaptive with lightweight or predictive with formal automatically. Choose the level from project evidence.
